title: FIV — feline immunodeficiency virus Coverage Audit
standfirst: FIV is the lentivirus of domestic cats and of wild felids — bobcat, puma and others, each with its own long-diverged lineage. Five features, all collinear, with rev recognised in the vocabulary but deliberately not declared: it is spliced, and this module calls no spliced feature.

sections.title: What the module calls
sections.lede: Five features, four of them called on every exemplar.

blocks.html: gag, pol, env and vif are called on 39 of 39 exemplars. orfA is the only variable one and carries no copy_num.

sections.title: Where it does not call, and why

blocks.html: orfA at 64.1% is a host-lineage split, not a truncation. Domestic-cat genomes call it 21 of 21; bobcat 0 of 10 and puma 3 of 6. Those same genomes call gag, pol, vif and env 39 of 39, so the absence is profile divergence on a small accessory gene rather than incomplete sequence. Widening orfA to reach the wild felids is a build decision, not a defect.

94.8% of the 673 deposited features from this module's taxa are bound by a naming rule. The remainder are recorded in UNASSIGNED and DISCARDED: the first is vocabulary no rule reached, the second is records the source itself calls partial or truncated, which the project discards rather than trains on.

sections.title: Vocabulary saturation
sections.lede: How fast each vocabulary stops growing as genomes are added.

blocks.html: The deposited vocabulary keeps growing; the module's does not. At the depth both reach, 32.9 distinct source strings correspond to 5.0 controlled annotations, a 6.6-fold collapse. The module reaches 95% of its final vocabulary after 14 proteins against the source's 174.

Coverage is measured by annotating de-replicated exemplars through the real GTO pipeline — annotate_by_viral_pssm-GTO.pl, then the transcript-edit and splice passes, then viral_genome_quality.pl — not by a reimplementation. Spliced features are included, which the flat feature-table path cannot represent. Rates are per exemplar, and exemplars are clustered at 95% nucleotide identity, so one row is one distinct sequence rather than one deposit.

source_note: Measured 27 October 2026 from the shipped module: the FIV block of Viral_PSSM.json, its profiles and collections, and the 27 October coverage re-annotation over 39 exemplars de-replicated from 265 genomes. Vocabulary figures come from collections/synonyms.tsv, written by the module's own builder from the naming rules, and count deposited features rather than unique sequences.
